items.question: The next build step (PD233(k)) adds the frame pool between the camera loop 1.1 and tracking loop 1.2: 20 image slots, and when all 20 are waiting, 1.1 skips reading the NEWEST camera frame. So under sustained overload tracking works through older queued frames (up to 20 behind, ~0.2 s at 90 Hz) and the newest frames are the ones lost. Your 2026-09-15 rule (docs/decisions.md:25) says the opposite: discard the backlog and take the newest frame. Every frame keeps its own buffer number, so timing labels stay correct either way; what differs is which frames are lost and how far tracking lags. Which do you want?
options: latest-wins as decided on 09-15: when tracking falls behind, it drops the queued older frames and takes the newest (the pool stage is changed to do that)
keep the planned pool: skip the newest read when 20 are waiting (lag up to 20 frames, oldest kept)
other (please say)
items.recommendation: latest-wins (your 09-15 rule); the build of the pool itself can proceed and the overload branch is set by your answer before the first real run
items.answer: ALREADY DECIDED by the user 2026-09-15 (memory prefer_the_freshest_frame_over_a_complete_backlog; docs/decisions.md:25), re-confirmed 2026-09-28 15:3x ("위에 프레임 관련해서는 내가 말한 내용이 있음 ... 우선순위가 있는데"). Priority: (1) NO CORRUPTION - image memory and its buffer number change together and the consumer verifies them; a pixel/number mismatch is data corruption. (2) LATEST-WINS - discard the queued backlog, read the newest frame (time-series rigor); a gap recorded by the buffer number is fine. (3) FALLBACK - if 1 and 2 cannot be made provably safe, acquisition and tracking may stay in ONE sequential loop. So the planned full=>skip-newest branch is WRONG and must become latest-wins with the buffer-number check, or the fallback.
